label: early original-phase token after a p/1 then p/digit bigram
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.02% of steps). 99% of mass is in the original (input) phase, peaking at t=3 (46% of mass), never at t<2, almost never in delimiter/copy steps. The strongest cue is the input two steps back being p or 1 (prev2_tok p: 20x lift, 1: 11x; together 78% of mass), usually with the previous input also p or a digit 0-2 (typical contexts: "p 1 _", "x 1 o p _", "f 1 2 _"). Current token is usually a first occurrence, enriched for 3, u, d, 0. Activation grows with the number of digits in the sequence. The predicate (p/1 two back, p/digit one back, original phase) covers ~67% of activation mass on dev but precision is only ~4%: most such contexts do not fire, and adding conditions on the current token raises precision only to ~13% while losing recall. So the context is necessary-ish but far from sufficient. Magnitude does not vary much (median 0.12, max 0.22); the top-quartile examples are covered slightly more often than the lowest quartile (83% vs 74%).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=p (+3.87), prev2_tok=p (+3.74), prev_tok=0 (+3.47), orig1=p (+3.06), orig0=w (+3.05), orig2=1 (+2.97). Lower it: phase=2 (-3.29), in_tok=1 (-3.19), prev3_tok=e (-2.95), in_tok=h (-2.88).
